newsitem.title: USA: CSX to spend $220 mln on Ohio-Chicago link.
newsitem.headline: CSX to spend $220 mln on Ohio-Chicago link.

text.p: CSX Corp plans to spend about $220 million to improve and expand capacity on 270 miles of its former Baltimore & Ohio route between Greenwich, Ohio, and Chicago, chief executive John W. Snow said Monday.

The section of railroad being upgraded and expanded links Conrail Inc's "Water Level Route" developed by its predcessor railroad, the New York Central, which connects Cleveland and the key eastern markets of Boston, New York and Philadelphia, with the industrial heartland of America and CSX's Chicago gateway to and from the West, he said.

"This is one of the most ambitious U.S. rail freight development ventures in modern times," Snow told a news conference. "This major construction project will create a truly world-class stretch of railroad with enormous economic potential not only for CSX, but also for Ohio."
He called the project "critical to realizing the growth objectives we have for our acquisition of Conrail lines."

Snow said the project will result in improved service and vastly increased capacity across this key line, which is the most direct route from New England and Mid-Atlantic coast ports and industrial centers to the Midwest.
A.R. "Pete" Carpenter, chief executive of CSX Transportation Inc, the company's rail unit, said work in Ohio, Indiana and Illinois will begin immediately and will be completed in early 1998.
He said Sverdrup Civil Inc of St. Louis has been retained as the general design/build contractor, and Harmon Industries Inc will provide the signaling services.
The 1997 phase, Carpenter said, includes construction of more than 70 route miles of double and triple track railroad, with an additional 40 route miles completed in 1998.

Ultimately, throughout the region, more than 100 route miles of new tract will be constructed and another 250 route miles of existing track will be reconstructed and upgraded or surfaced. The project will involve installation of cross-overs and signaling systems that will allow reverse operation over all tracks, Carpenter said.

In addition, more than a dozen new connections will be installed to smooth traffic flows on the CSX system and to facilitate interchange of traffic with short lines, regional carriers and other railroads serving the region.

Carpenter said that CSXT will be implementing an extensive public information and highway grade crossing safety campaign all along the Ohio route. Additionally, he said, the railroad will promptly begin working with state and local economic development offices, making certain they have all of the information they need to promote economic development and bring new industries to Ohio and the region.
